newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crude - EFP premium strong, grades ease.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crude - EFP premium strong, grades ease.

text.p: U.S. cash crude trading early Thursday held the pattern seen all week, with July exchange-for-physicals (EFPs) premium staying strong in anticipation of another high delivery of foreign crude against the future, while grade differentials were under pressure as outright prices rose.
"Deals have been getting done, there is some back and forth trading but everyone says there is plenty of crude around and you can see the diffs are seeing some pressure," said one Houston broker.

Benchmark West Texas Intermediate/Cushing rose sharply with futures after the July contract saw heavy buying by speculative funds at $20.57 and above. Cash WTI/Cushing maintained a premium of between 10 and 15 cents in line with the EFP premium and was around $21.20 at midday.

Traders said that those delivered the 2.349 million barrels of Nigerian Bonny Light on the June contract, particulary Morgan Stanley Group Inc's oil trading unit which took delivery of 1.392 million barrels, are expected to deliver on the July contract. Also, there was talk that an oil major had bought another load of Bonny Light which it was also likely to delivery on July.
Among the grades, Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James traded at eight cents over WTI/Cushing Thursday, having fallen steadily from a 20 cent premium a week ago.
WTI/Midland was at 38/34 cents under WTI/Cushing, having sold at 35 cents under benchmark WTI Wednesday.
The American Petroleum Institute reported on Wednesday that crude runs were up 100,000 barrels per day (bpd) last week and refinery capacity was running at nearly 97 percent.
But crude supply still is ample, traders said, with supply from Gulf of Mexico, Latin America, Asia and Alaska North Slope heading east down the pipeline.
